title: Building a linear model from a context
keyIdea: When something changes by the same amount for every equal step, a straight line models it: output = start value + rate × input. Get the rate from two readings as change in output ÷ change in input, work back to input 0 for the start value, then say which inputs the model makes sense for.

kid: A candle burns down at a steady speed. After 2 hours it is 18 cm tall. After 5 hours it is 12 cm tall.
From 2 hours to 5 hours is 3 hours. In that time it got 6 cm shorter. So it loses 6 ÷ 3 = 2 cm each hour.
Now go back to when it was lit. That is 2 hours before the first reading, so add 2 × 2 = 4 cm. It started at 22 cm.
So the height is 22 take away 2 for every hour: h = 22 − 2t. At 11 hours the candle is gone, so the rule only works up to 11 hours.
adult: A context is linear when equal steps in the input give equal changes in the output: a steady burn, a fixed hourly charge, a spring stretching the same amount per kilogram. The model is y = a + bx, where b is the rate and a is the start value (the output when x = 0).

With two readings (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂), the rate is b = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁), in output units per input unit. Then work back from either reading: a = y₁ − b × x₁. Check the model against the other reading before you trust it.

Read the numbers in context. In C = 35 + 20m for a gym, 35 is the joining fee in pounds and 20 is the cost per month. A falling quantity has a negative rate. A model also has a sensible range: h = 22 − 2t gives negative heights after 11 hours, so it only holds for 0 ≤ t ≤ 11.

Common mistakes: using the first reading given as the start value; dividing one reading by its input (for example 18 ÷ 2), which wrongly assumes the output was 0 at the start; forgetting to divide the change by the number of steps; getting the sign of the rate wrong; and using the model far outside the range of the data.

familyTip: Fill a jug from a tap that runs steadily and note the water level at two times, such as 10 s and 25 s. Work out the rise per second, then work back to see if the jug really started empty. Does your rule predict the level at 20 s?

worked.title: A tank drains steadily. After 3 min it holds 340 L; after 8 min it holds 240 L. Build a model and say when it is empty.
steps: Change in volume: 240 − 340 = −100 L. Change in time: 8 − 3 = 5 min.
Rate = −100 ÷ 5 = −20 L per minute. It is negative because the tank is emptying.
Start value: work back 3 minutes from the first reading: 340 + 3 × 20 = 400 L. So V = 400 − 20t.
Check: at t = 8, V = 400 − 160 = 240 L. ✓ Empty when 400 − 20t = 0, so t = 20. The model holds for 0 ≤ t ≤ 20.

practice.prompt: A candle burns steadily. After {x} h it is {=s-r*x} cm tall. After {=x+d} h it is {=s-r*(x+d)} cm tall. How many cm does it lose each hour?
practice.hint: Change in height ÷ change in time. The time changed by {d} hours.
practice.explain: It lost {=r*d} cm in {d} hours, so the rate is {=r*d} ÷ {d} = {r} cm per hour (a rate of −{r} in the model).

practice.prompt: A plumber charges a call-out fee plus a fixed amount per hour. A 2-hour job costs £{=c+2*r}. A 4-hour job costs £{=c+4*r}. What is the call-out fee in pounds?
practice.hint: First find the cost per hour: (£{=c+4*r} − £{=c+2*r}) ÷ 2. Then work back from the 2-hour job.

practice.prompt: A gym costs £95 for 3 months and £175 for 7 months, including a joining fee. Which model fits?
practice.hint: Rate = (175 − 95) ÷ (7 − 3). Then work back 3 months from £95.

practice.prompt: A spring's length is L = 13 + 3m cm, where m is the mass hung on it in kg. What does the 13 mean?
choices: The length with no mass on it
How much it stretches per kg
The length with 1 kg on it
practice.explain: When m = 0, L = 13. So 13 cm is the natural length. The 3 is the stretch per kg.

practice.prompt: A candle's height is h = 30 − 3t cm after t hours. For which times does the model make sense?
practice.explain: 30 − 3t = 0 when t = 10. After that the model gives negative heights, which cannot happen.

pool.prompt: After 2 h a candle is 18 cm. After 5 h it is 12 cm. Zoe says it loses 9 cm per hour, because 18 ÷ 2 = 9. What went wrong?
choices: She divided one reading by its time; use change ÷ change: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 cm per hour
Nothing, 9 cm per hour is right
pool.hint: How much height was lost between the two readings, and over how long?
pool.explain: 18 ÷ 2 assumes the candle started at 0 cm. Between the readings it lost 6 cm in 3 h, so the rate is 2 cm per hour.

pool.prompt: A spring is 19 cm long with 2 kg hanging on it, and 28 cm long with 5 kg. It stretches steadily. How long is it with nothing hanging on it, in cm?
pool.hint: Stretch per kg = (28 − 19) ÷ (5 − 2). Then take 2 kg worth off 19 cm.
pool.explain: Rate = 9 ÷ 3 = 3 cm per kg. Start = 19 − 2 × 3 = 13 cm. So L = 13 + 3m.

pool.prompt: On one day the air is 9 °C at 1 km up and −4 °C at 3 km up, falling steadily. What is the rate of change?
pool.hint: Change in temperature ÷ change in height. Is the temperature going up or down?
pool.explain: (−4 − 9) ÷ (3 − 1) = −13 ÷ 2 = −6.5 °C per km. It is negative because it gets colder higher up.

pool.prompt: A tank drains so that V = {=r*n} − {r}t litres after t minutes. After how many minutes is it empty?
pool.explain: {r}t = {=r*n}, so t = {=r*n} ÷ {r} = {n} minutes. After that the model would give negative volumes.

pool.prompt: Ana saves the same amount each week. After 3 weeks she has £47. After 8 weeks she has £87. Which model fits?
pool.hint: Rate = (87 − 47) ÷ 5. Then go back 3 weeks from £47.
pool.explain: Rate = 40 ÷ 5 = £8 per week. Start = 47 − 3 × 8 = £23, money she had before she began. 23 + 64 = 87. ✓

pool.prompt: A phone plays video. After {a} h it has {=b-k*a}% battery. After {=a+3} h it has {=b-k*(a+3)}%. How many percentage points does it lose per hour?
pool.hint: The battery fell by {=3*k} points in 3 hours.
pool.explain: {=3*k} ÷ 3 = {k} points per hour, so the rate is −{k} in the model.

pool.prompt: A model for phone battery is B = 92 − 8t. It predicts B = −4 at t = 12. What does that tell you?
choices: The model no longer makes sense; the phone is flat at t = 11.5
pool.hint: Can battery go below 0%? When does B reach 0?
pool.explain: 92 − 8t = 0 at t = 11.5. Past that, the model gives impossible values, so it only holds for 0 ≤ t ≤ 11.5.

pool.prompt: Which of these can be modelled well by a straight line?
choices: A pool filling from a hose at 15 L per minute
Savings that earn 5% interest each year
The height of a ball that is thrown up
pool.hint: Look for the same change for every equal step.
pool.explain: The hose adds 15 L every minute, the same each step. Interest grows by more each year, and a ball slows, stops and falls, so neither is linear.

visual.caption: Slide t. The candle model h = 22 − 2t: start at 22 cm, lose 2 cm each hour. Past t = 11 the answer turns negative and the model stops making sense.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: get the rate from two candle readings, work back to the start, build the model, find where it stops, then model a gym.
